versions: the TypeScript ∪ JavaScript ∪ JSX union, every TS version through 5.x syntax (satisfies, const type params, accessor, infer constraints, template literal types, import attributes) in ONE parser
dialect_decision: One parser for TS + JS + JSX. The DESIGN.md §4.2 dialect split existed for the `<T>` ambiguity, and this ledger previously justified skipping it by measuring angle-bracket CASTS at zero incidence in the top-300. That measurement was right and the conclusion was wrong: the top-1000 corpus has 11+ files of GENERIC ARROW FUNCTIONS (`const f = <T extends X>(x: T) => x`, in zod and rxjs), which hit the same ambiguity and are ordinary modern style. They now parse in the single grammar. The fix was not precedence but a token collision: `_jsx_identifier` and `identifier` matched the same text, so the LEXER chose JSX before the parser could fork — the same trap the rust ledger records for identifier/type_identifier. With plain JSX names lexing as the ordinary identifier and only dashed names getting their own token, GLR forks and jsx_opening_element's negative dynamic precedence yields to the arrow whenever both complete. Casts remain a ledgered gap at 0 measured files.

oracles.tool: tools/js-oracle under node (V8 via vm, CJS/ESM picked by module rules, @babel/parser leg for JSX)
oracles.role: judges .js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs — deliberately NOT the TypeScript parser, which would bless TS syntax in .js files

corpus.source: top-1000 npm packages by download rank, both corpora (typescript: .ts/.tsx; javascript: .js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx, minified excluded)
corpus.blind_to: npm ships mostly compiled .js + .d.ts, so the TS corpus is declaration-file-heavy (undici-types, type-fest) and light on application .ts; JSX incidence is low outside React-adjacent packages
corpus.mutation_falsification: javascript with while_statement deleted from _loop: 429 gap files (vs 8). typescript with the _type_member_end token removed: 20 gap files (vs 13). Both the oldest and the newest rules can be falsified.
corpus.widening_note: Widened from the top-300 to the top-1000: typescript 1,598 -> 11,988 files, javascript 4,801 -> 25,297. It found six real families the narrow corpus had no instance of, the largest of which invalidates a claim this ledger used to make (see dialect_decision).

known_gaps.construct: a parameter NAMED `never`/`unknown`/`symbol` inside a bare function type, e.g. `(symbol: ts.Symbol) => boolean`
known_gaps.note: TypeScript reserves none of the three, so this is valid. Giving them an identifier reading fixes it and breaks `expectTypeOf<t1>().toEqualTypeOf<unknown>()` far worse: the identifier reading creates a competing generic-arrow fork that wins and the type-argument reading dies. Measured 10 -> 23 gap files. Held as a gap deliberately.

known_gaps.construct: ambient `declare class C { clear(): void\n [Symbol.iterator]: ... }` — a bodyless method followed by an index signature
known_gaps.note: `class_body` separates members by nothing, because an ordinary method ends in `}`. An ambient method ends in a TYPE, so `void` and the next `[` merge into one indexed_access_type. Adding `optional($._type_member_end)` to `class_body` generates cleanly but the token is never offered in that state, with or without the scanner's ASI guard. Both files are undici-types.
the dialect-split construct; one file in 11,988. Accepted as a gap by design — see dialect_decision.

known_gaps.construct: a generic arrow whose type parameter carries an `extends` constraint at the head of a call argument

deviations.what: one parser instead of the typescript/tsx dialect pair; JSX is grammatical in .ts files (tsc rejects it there) — union-widening traded for a single table, justified by the zero measured cast incidence

class methods are function_definition (python/rust precedent: same construct, same name), class members route through _declaration so a method answers (_declaration), (_member) and the _callable facet alike

ASI is a static continuation set in the scanner (the flip side of the hazard list: ( [ ` + - * / % < > = & | ^ ? : , . in instanceof as satisfies extends), with ++/-- forcing insertion; spec-ASI's can-the-parse-continue rule is approximated, which costs exactly the one ledgered hazard file

expression statements exclude function/class/{ at the first position structurally — the JS spec rule, enforced in the grammar rather than by dynamic precedence (which measured as unable to win the fork)

`T?` is a tuple-ELEMENT form, not a general type. TS only allows it there, and admitting it to the type tier let `x < -1 ? p : q` fork into a type-argument reading that outlived the expression one — 3 corpus files.

`void`, `never`, `unknown` and `symbol` are a predefined_type node rather than identifiers. `void` is a unary operator, so it can never arrive as an identifier and `f<void>()` previously had no reading at all.

object-type members are separated by a scanner token (_type_member_end) as well as , and ;. It carries ASI's continuation set with exactly one token flipped: `[` CONTINUES an expression (`foo` newline `[0]` is a subscript) and BEGINS a type member (an index signature). That single difference is why it is a separate token rather than reusing ASI, and it is what finally closed the 5-file .d.ts family — a precedence attempt had regressed 20 files, and a first version of this token with NO continuation set regressed to 100 by severing every multi-line member type.

`string` is a `_literal` here and is NOT one in python, and that asymmetry is correct rather than a drift: typescript's string is a single token that cannot interpolate, so it satisfies the vocabulary's per-rule test ('determined by its own text, for EVERY instance of the rule'), while python's `string` rule carries f-strings and so cannot. It was excluded here by oversight until vocabulary 0.3.0 measured it. The `_string` facet exists because of exactly this: `(_literal)` is not comparable across languages for strings, and `(_string)` is.

deviations.construct: `x as A & B` / `x as A | B`
deviations.was: `union_type` and `intersection_type` sat at prec 2 and 3, below PREC.cast (15), so the parser reduced `as_expression` at the operator and read the rest as a bitwise-and/or over an object literal. `x as A & B` produced `(x as A) & B`.
deviations.now: both operators sit above `cast` (`&` still tighter than `|`), giving `as_expression(intersection_type(A, B))`.
deviations.note: SILENT: the wrong tree is well-formed, so the sweep never flagged it. Only `x as A & { c?: B }` errored, because `?` is illegal in an object literal. Found by chasing that one file.

deviations.construct: `a(): asserts this is X` inside an object type
deviations.was: `asserts` was reachable as a bare type name, so the member looked complete after it and `_type_member_end` was valid there. The external scanner is not forked by GLR, so it cut the member and the predicate reading died before the parser saw it — shredding into four bogus property_signatures.
deviations.now: `asserts` and `is` reach identifier position only, via `_value_word`; `predicate_type` now requires `asserts` or `is` rather than deriving a bare name.
deviations.note: SILENT for the same reason: four property_signatures is well-formed. Only the generic form `asserts this is X<Y>` errored.

deviations.construct: a comment between two object-type members
deviations.was: the scanner skipped whitespace and then judged by the next character; a comment starts with `/`, which is in both continuation sets, so the boundary was suppressed and `void /*c*/ [Symbol.iterator]` became one indexed_access_type.
deviations.now: `skip_trivia` skips line and block comments too, and counts a line terminator inside a block comment as crossed.
deviations.note: no corpus file exercises the interface form; committed as a correctness fix, not a number.

roles_note: 21 of 22 table-tier terms thread — _control_flow nests in _statement (like python, unlike rust's expression-orientation), _member routes through _declaration in class bodies, _modifier has seven members (accessibility/readonly/static/abstract/override/declare/accessor: TS is the most modifier-rich language yet). _clause was the one unthreadable term — the third language to record the same evidence — and MOVED to the facet tier in vocabulary 0.2.0, with seven members here (else/case/default/finally/catch/import/export clauses).
